intro: Vale do Pereiro maps one tree: the Sobreira Grande, the Big Cork Oak, Portugal's Tree of the Year 2022 and third in Europe the same year on 70,563 votes. It stands on a path at the edge of the village in open montado, in Arraiolos municipality, about 22 kilometres north of Evora, and its wide canopy is where walkers, field workers and herds stop for shade.

question_meta: Vale do Pereiro's mapped tree is the Sobreira Grande, a cork oak that was Portugal's Tree of the Year 2022 and third in Europe.
question_answer: The tree mapped at Vale do Pereiro is the Sobreira Grande, the Big Cork Oak, Portugal's Tree of the Year 2022, which came third in European Tree of the Year 2022 on 70,563 votes. It stands on a path at the edge of the village in Arraiolos municipality, about 22 kilometres north of Evora, and the contest page gives its age as about 250 years.
question_context: The Sobreira Grande was nominated by the municipality of Arraiolos for the 2022 contest run by UNAC, the Mediterranean forest union, and won the Portuguese round before finishing third in Europe on 70,563 votes. The contest page makes its case on shade rather than size: walkers, the people working the surrounding fields at their summer lunch, and herds all stop under its wide canopy, which spreads over a path at the edge of the village in open montado. Its age, about 250 years, is the nominator's figure with no measurement published behind it, and no source we have read gives a girth or a height. The Arraiolos council said in 2022 that it would seek Tree of Public Interest status; we have not seen that granted. Walking apps list a circular route named after the tree, roughly nine to eleven kilometres with little shade. There is no useful public transport from Evora, 22 kilometres to the south, so it is a day trip by car.

trees.story:
In 2022, 70,563 people voted for a cork oak on a path outside a small Alentejo village, and it still came third in Europe. At home it had already won. The Sobreira Grande, the Big Cork Oak, was Portugal's Tree of the Year 2022, nominated by the municipality of Arraiolos in the contest run by UNAC, the Mediterranean forest union.

The case the contest page makes is not a record. It is shade. The tree stands on a path at Vale do Pereiro, in open montado, and its wide canopy is where walkers stop, where the people working the fields around it eat their lunch in summer, and where the herds wait out the heat.

How long it has done that is less certain. The contest page gives its age as about 250 years. That is the nominator's figure, with no measurement published behind it, and no source we have read gives a girth or a height either. Treat it as the village's estimate rather than a count of rings. The same year, the Arraiolos council said it would seek national protection as a Tree of Public Interest. We have not seen that it was granted.

Vale do Pereiro is about 22 kilometres north of Évora, and you will want a car. Walking apps list a circular route named after the tree, roughly nine to eleven kilometres with little shade on the way, which makes its one job easy to appreciate at the end.

trees.access: Stands on a path at the edge of the village of Vale do Pereiro, in open montado; no entry fee or gate reported. Marked circular walk PR4 ARL 'Rota da Sobreira Grande' (about 9 to 11 km, little shade) per Wikiloc/Komoot listings, not an official page. Land ownership not stated by any source; confirm with Arraiolos tourist office (turismo@cm-arraiolos.pt) if needed.
trees.transport: About 22 km north of Evora by road, no useful public transport reported; Arraiolos town is reached by bus from Evora, then the village is a further car or taxi hop. Day trip by car.

No girth or height found in any fetched source. Flagged: one fetched source (contest page, nominator-supplied) plus alive observation; second source for age not fetched. Not the Sobreiro Assobiador.
